meter.title: Wattendix
meter.description: Only the home's consumption is required; everything else is optional and can be changed later. Start by telling how this measurement reaches Home Assistant.

data_description.source_mode: Live: a clamp, a panel module, the meter's local port. Delayed: data from the grid operator or your supplier, arriving the next day; Wattendix then tracks day, week, month and year, without the current hour.
data_description.price_mode: Without a price, everything is tracked in kWh. "One price per sensor" fits when peak and off-peak each have their own sensor.
data_description.subscription_mode: Ignored without a price. Spread over the days of the month.

source.title: Consumption measurement
source.description: Pick what measures the home's consumption. Several items are added together: peak index + off-peak index, three phases, several meters. Live: energy counters (Wh, kWh, MWh) or power sensors (W, kW); a counter is more reliable, it catches up what was used while Home Assistant was stopped. With solar, pick the grid import counter.

data_description.source: Sensors, or statistics if you chose imported statistics.
data_description.max_power: A little above your contract's power. A counter jump that would exceed it over the elapsed time is rejected (counter reset, absurd value).

price.title: Electricity price
price.description:
The price is applied to energy when it is counted: changing rates never recomputes the past.

{sources}

data.price_entity: Entity giving the price per kWh

data_description.offpeak_ranges: One or more ranges separated by commas, for example 23:10-07:11 or 01:00-07:00, 12:30-14:30.
data_description.price_entity: Its state must be the current price of one kWh. The last known value is kept while it is unavailable.

data_description.subscription_entity: The last known value is kept while the entity is unavailable.

weather.title: Weather
weather.description: Optional. With an outdoor temperature, Wattendix learns how much the home uses depending on the weather and sharpens its estimates. Best is to give both: the thermometer to learn from history, the weather entity for forecasts.

heating.title: Heating
heating.description: Optional. With the heat pump's consumption, Wattendix compares it to what is expected for how cold it has been (degree-days).

data.season_month: First month of the heating season

data_description.heat_pump: Energy counters or power sensors, added together (several heaters or units). Leave empty to skip.
data_description.hdd_base: Outdoor temperature below which the home starts heating.

error.bad_unit: Unsupported unit: Wh, kWh, MWh, W or kW is required.
error.bad_daily_unit: A daily reading must be an energy: Wh, kWh or MWh.
error.bad_statistic: Unusable statistic: a cumulative energy in Wh, kWh or MWh is required.
error.too_many_sources: One price per sensor is limited to 6 sensors.
error.delayed_price: Delayed data only gives one total per day: time ranges cannot apply. Use a flat rate, or one price per sensor if peak and off-peak are separate.
